identity.title: The ALMA survey to Resolve exoKuiper belt Substructures (ARKS): IV. CO gas imaging and overview

paper_type_evidence.quote: The ALMA survey to Resolve exoKuiper belt Substructures (ARKS) is the first ALMA large program to target debris discs at high spectro-spatial resolution.

question.value: What is the spectro-spatial distribution, optical depth and mass of CO gas in ARKS debris discs, and is CO detectable in the 13 discs without previous detections?

evidence.quote: in order to analyse the spectro-spatial distribution of CO and constrain the gas mass in discs that were known to host gas previously, and to search for gas in the remaining 13 discs
ARKS, project number 2022.1.00338.L, PI: S. Marino

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 12CO J=3-2 at 26 m/s resolution (gas-bearing) or 846 m/s (gas-free); 13CO at 886 m/s

evidence.quote: the spectral resolution was set to 26 m s$^{-1}$ (the finest spectral resolution possible with ALMA) for the $^{12}$CO spectral window and to 886 m s$^{-1}$ for the $^{13}$CO spectral window
the spectral windows containing the $^{12}$CO line (rest frequency of 345.796 GHz) and the $^{13}$CO line (rest frequency of 330.599 GHz)
the spectral windows containing the $^{12}$CO line (rest frequency of 345.796 GHz) and the $^{13}$CO line (rest frequency of 330.599 GHz)

evidence.quote: the imaging pipeline led to beam sizes ranging from 70 to 150 mas (corresponding to physical scales projected on the sky of 8 to 16 au) for $^{12}$CO
The RMS levels in the $^{12}$CO cubes ranged between 3 to 5 mJy/beam and from 0.6 to 1.0 mJy/beam in the $^{13}$CO cubes

method.value: Quadratic fit to peak velocity; peak brightness temperature via Planck; spectro-spatial shifted integrated intensity

evidence.quote: we fit a quadratic function to the peak and its two neighbouring channels in each of the pixels’ spectra

analysis_steps.goal: Search for CO in gas-free discs by stacking

method.value: Spectro-spatial shifting/stacking of dirty cubes in both rotation directions; 3 sigma upper limits from 7 km/s bootstrapped windows

evidence.quote: We spectrally integrated over 7 km s$^{-1}$ wide noisy regions, located in random regions of each spectrum

evidence.quote: under the assumption of Keplerian rotation and that the CO emission is co-located with the dust emission

method.value: Integrate stacked spectrum over V*±5 sigma (Gaussian fit); box integration for edge-on; optically thin LTE mass and tau=77 scaling

evidence.quote: We set the limits of integration to $V_{*} \pm 5~\sigma$.

results_numeric.quantity: Velocity-based upper limits on 12CO inner radius

evidence.quote: We calculated velocity-based upper limits to the inner disc radii of $3 - 68$ au.

results_numeric.quantity: Planet mass opening gap in HD 131488 (lower limit)

evidence.quote: We find that a $7 M_\oplus$ planet located at 5.8 au is capable of opening a gap

findings_qualitative.value: CO is broader than and peaks interior to the mm dust in all five gas-bearing discs; no 12CO detected in the 13 gas-free discs

evidence.quote: In each disc, the CO peaks interior to the dust, although the offset between the dust and gas varies with each system.

claims.hypothesis: Is CO radially co-located with dust?
claims.experiment: Radial profiles of 12CO/13CO vs ARKS continuum
claims.result: CO peaks interior to the dust and is more extended
claims.finding: Second-generation scenario requires significant shielding to viscously spread

evidence.quote: in each of the gas-bearing discs, the CO intensity distribution peaks interior to the millimetre-sized dust grains

claims.hypothesis: Is 12CO optically thick with optically thin 13CO?
claims.result: Ratios flat with radius in four of five discs
claims.finding: Both isotopologues thick or both thin; thick-12CO/thin-13CO ruled out for four

evidence.quote: we rule out that $^{12}$CO is optically thick and co-located with optically thin $^{13}$CO.

claims.hypothesis: Do gas-free discs host detectable CO?

evidence.quote: Despite application of the S/N-boosting spectro-spatial stacking technique, we do not detect $^{12}$CO in any of the systems.

claims.hypothesis: Does gas detection correlate with age/fractional luminosity?
claims.result: Detections mostly in young systems but large scatter

evidence.quote: no trend is present within detected systems

why_this_method.value: Keplerian masks needed because of >1000 channels at 13 m/s

evidence.quote: manual masking is unfeasible and masks covering the gas emission in every channel have to be defined automatically

limitations_admitted.value: Optically thick masses are lower limits; inner radii are upper limits; degeneracy thick/thin needs radiative transfer

evidence.quote: To break this degeneracy, radiative transfer modelling needs to be carried out

Different spectral resolution for 12CO and 13CO affects ratios
